events.description: 32. ORDER. The Motion to Quash at ECF No. 24 is GRANTED IN PART. Pursuant to Rule 4.4(g) of the Puerto Rico Rules of Civil Procedure, P.R. Laws Ann. t. 32, App. V, made applicable through Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(j)(2)(B), plaintiff must serve a copy of the complaint and summons directed at the defendant, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico Planning Board, on the Commonwealth's Secretary of Justice. That did not happen. In addition, the copy of the executed summons submitted by the Planning Board with its motion to quash does not clearly evince that service was properly made under Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(j)(2)(A) (by "delivering a copy of the summons and of the complaint to its chief executive officer"). Plaintiff's response to the motion to quash and the Court's show cause order addresses none of these omissions and relies on inapplicable case law. Accordingly, plaintiff is ORDERED to complete service on the Planning Board by no later than 12/10/2025, and notify the Court by even date. Failure to do so may result in the imposition of sanctions, up to and including dismissal of the complaint against the Planning Board. Signed by Judge Aida M. Delgado-Colon on 12/05/2025. events.description: 39. ORDER re 36 Motion In Compliance NOTED. 37 Motion to Stay GRANTED IN PART, DENIED IN PART. It appears that plaintiff has recently completed service upon the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico Planning Board under Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(j)(2)(B), by serving a copy of the summons and complaint on the Commonwealth's Secretary of Justice. ECF No. 36. Non-compliance with this step was the only ground raised by the Planning Board in its motion to quash and no other defect in service was alluded to. ECF No. 24. To be clear, in partly granting said motion, the Court stated that it was not evident that the alternative method of service provided for in Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(j)(2)(A) had been met, but did so as a way of assuring itself that it could not deem the Planning Board served as per the facts and documents before it at the time. That is why, given the Planning Board's limited grounds for quashing service, the Court ordered completion of service rather than re-service. The Planning Board has been on notice of the claims against it since at least October 29, 2025, when it requested a 41-day extension of time to answer the complaint. ECF No. 6. The amended complaint filed on November 24, 2025, is identical to the original complaint (save for a technical modification ordered by the Court (ECF No. 21)) and includes a request for preliminary injunctive relief, which was re-filed as a motion as per the Court's order. ECF No. 5. The Planning Board received electronic notifications of all these developments through counsel and thus has had adequate notice for purposes of Fed. R. Civ. P. 65. The Court sees no reason to stay proceedings. The Magistrate Judge controls all scheduling matters and extensions of time related to the preliminary injunction request, as per the referral order, but need not feel compelled to modify the schedule on account of the reasons set forth in the Planning Board's motion. The motion to stay is DENIED. The deadline to respond to the motion for preliminary injunction remains set for 12/15/2025 unless otherwise modified by the Magistrate Judge. Notwithstanding, the Court will GRANT the Planning Board until 12/30/2025 to answer the amended complaint or otherwise plead, as requested. Signed by Judge Aida M. Delgado-Colon on 12/11/2025. (idg) (Entered: 12/11/2025)

events.description: 54. Minute Entry for proceedings held before US Magistrate Judge Giselle Lopez-Soler: Status and Argumentative Hearing held on 12/18/2025. Present for Plaintiffs was Atty. Jose Valenzuela-Alvarado. Present for Defendants were Attys. Diana Perez-Carlo, Lavinia Aparicio-Lopez, Damaris Quinones-Vargas and Javier Vega-Villalba. events.description: 86. ORDER. The Motion to Strike at ECF No. 73 is GRANTED. Plaintiff's filing at ECF No. 70 is ordered STRICKEN for failure to comply with Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a). Putting aside whether or not plaintiff has already amended the complaint once as a matter of course, the fact remains that more than 21 days have elapsed since plaintiff was notified of defendants' several Rule 12(b)(6) motions, the last of which was filed on December 30, 2025. ECF Nos. 30, 34, 46, 55. Accordingly, as per the plaint text of Rule 15(a)(1)(B), plaintiff cannot avail herself of the opportunity amend as a matter of course, assuming she even had that right. Frankly, the Court is baffled that plaintiffs 13-page, same-day response to the motion to strike (ECF No. 77) considers defendants position "frivolous" when she all but admits non-compliance with the Rule. Further, a preliminary injunction hearing has already been held and the matter of whether plaintiff is entitled to injunctive relief remains sub judice before the Magistrate Judge. Accordingly, the Magistrate Judge shall take into account plaintiff's latest "supplemental" request at ECF Nos. 71, 72 in the rendering of her Report and Recommendation. Once the forthcoming Report and Recommendation on the pending motions to dismiss and the requests for injunctive relief is issued, and once any objections thereto are made and resolved, plaintiff may renew her request leave to amend the complaint and justify its amendment, which will be considered under Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2) and relevant case law. Signed by Judge Aida M. Delgado-Colon on 2/12/2026. (wm) (Entered: 02/12/2026)
